title: A Renewal Uplift Waiver Across a Straddled Rule
scenario_text:
A deal desk analyst at Sycamore Grid must decide whether a multi-year contract can waive its annual uplift, given two prior decisions that straddle a rule change.

**Decision A (2024-01-22)**
Customer 'Ordell Utilities' | 3-year contract | had a service-credit incident in the prior term. Requested a waiver of the 4% annual uplift. DENIED. Note: 'Under the uplift policy then in effect, uplift waivers were granted only to customers with a clean service record in the prior term. Ordell had a service-credit incident, so the waiver was denied.'

**Decision B (2024-08-19)**
Customer 'Pell Energy' | 3-year contract | also had a prior service-credit incident. Requested the same waiver and it was APPROVED. Note: 'Under the revised uplift policy effective 2024-07-01, uplift waivers turn on committed contract term, not service history: any contract of 3 years or longer qualifies for a waiver. Pell qualified on term.'

**Current request C (2024-12-05)**
Customer 'Quillon Power' | 3-year contract | had a service-credit incident last term. Requests a waiver of the 4% annual uplift.

**Uplift Waiver Policy (current, effective 2024-07-01)**
Annual uplift waivers are granted to any contract with a committed term of 3 years or longer, regardless of prior service history. Service-credit incidents no longer disqualify a customer from a waiver. Term-based qualification has applied since July 1, 2024.

**Slack — #deal-desk**
AE: 'We denied Ordell's uplift waiver in January over a service-credit incident, and Quillon had one too. Same denial?'
Analyst: 'Ordell was under the old service-history rule. We approved Pell in August on term alone. Let me line Quillon up against the current policy.'

Quillon is a 3-year contract with a prior service-credit incident, just like Pell was.
question: How should the analyst handle Quillon Power's uplift-waiver request?
choices: Deny the waiver, consistent with the January denial of Ordell's waiver over a service-credit incident.

Approve the waiver, because the current rule grants a waiver to any 3-year-or-longer contract regardless of service history — so the August Pell approval, not the pre-July Ordell denial, is the governing precedent.
Escalate the waiver to VP Sales, since waiving uplift for a customer with a prior service-credit incident exceeds Deal Desk authority.
Waive only 2% of the 4% uplift as a compromise given the prior service-credit incident.
